newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow demands U.S. free ex-Soviet spy.
newsitem.headline: Moscow demands U.S. free ex-Soviet spy.

text.p: Russia demanded on Tuesday that the United States release a retired Soviet intelligence officer, calling his arrest in New York last month a "deliberate provocation" that could sour relations with Washington.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Mikhail Demurin told a news briefing Moscow had demanded the unconditional release of Vladimir Galkin, who was seized by the Federal Bureau of Investigation on arrival at Kennedy airport on October 29.
"A Russian citizen has become a victim of a deliberate provocation," Demurin told a news briefing.
"He must be immediately freed without any conditions. The case against him must be dropped.
"We believe that the U.S. side must understand that its irresponsible actions may have negative consequences for Russia-U.S. relations."

Moscow says Galkin was arrested on charges of being a former Soviet intelligence officer -- despite the fact that he had left the service in 1992 and had clearly stated his former profession in his application for a U.S. visa.
The case has angered Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) which sees it as a breach of an understanding between rival spy agencies not to hound retired intelligence officers.
SVR spokeswoman Tatyana Samolis warned Washington on Sunday the spy agency would retaliate unless Galkin is released.
"We don't intend to leave Vladimir Galkin to the mercy of fate," she said. "Our patience is not unlimited and an appropriate response will not be long in coming."
Political analysts have suggested that former senior Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) officers might be legitimate targets for retaliation while on private visits to Russia.
